newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity seen up on Ariz. nuke outage.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity seen up on Ariz. nuke outage.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures were expected to open stronger Tuesday on news of an outage at the 1,221 megawatt Palo Verde 1 nuclear power unit in Arizona, industry sources said.

Sources said it was difficult to estimate how much higher the futures would open, as over the counter values jumped significantly early in the day and then backed off on news the outage was expected to be short term.
"It took off really strong at first, but it's backing off now -- it is real choppy this morning," said one New York-based power trader.
June Palo Verde (PV) was reported to have traded as high as $26.75 per megawatt hour (MWh) in early over-the-counter action from a Friday NYMEX June futures close at $25.15 per MWh.
June California Oregon Border (COB) was pegged at $20.50-21.25 per MWh in over-the-counter discussion from Friday's NYMEX June COB futures close at $19.37 per MWh.
Arizona Public Service said Tuesday it expects to restore output at the Palo Verde nuclear power plant by late Wednesday or possibly earlier.

A total of about 7,000 megawatts (MW) of power generation remained off line in the West for either planned or unplanned maintenance. Much of the idled generation was expected to return to service over the next several weeks, however.
The 1,087 MW Diablo Canyon 1 nuclear unit was expected to begin production May 29 from a scheduled refueling and maintenance outage which began April 19.
Several coal-fired plants are also expected back at the end of month including the 750 MW Colstrip unit in Montana and 750 MW Four Corners unit in Arizona.
Restart of the 550 MW unit 2 at the Jim Bridger coal-fired generating complex in Wyoming was heard postponed to June 4 from this weekend.
Forecasters expect temperatures in the Southwest to be near-normal through much of the week and rise to one to five degrees above normal by the weekend, under partially cloudy skies.
The maximum temperature in Phoenix, Ariz., Tuesday was expected to be near 92 degrees Fahrenheit.

In the Pacific Northwest, temperatures were expected to be one to five degrees below normal through much of the week and then rise to one to five degrees above normal by the weekend. Sunny skies were expected through much of the week.
As of 1020 EDT, NYMEX June Henry Hub natural gas was trading up 1.5 cents at $2.30 per million British thermal units.
